Online Communities and Young Adults. Abstract. This conceptual paper discusses how online communities
support young adults. The aim is theoretical: we review prior literature and propose a framework linking
participation, trust and wellbeing. No new data are collected. Introduction. Researchers have studied forums,
groups and chat servers separately; this paper brings the strands together. Online Communities and Young

discusses how online communities support young adults. The aim is theoretical: we review prior literature and
propose a framework linking participation, trust and wellbeing. No new data are collected. Introduction.
Researchers have studied forums, groups and chat servers separately; this paper brings the strands together.
Framework. We distinguish three mechanisms: shared interest, mutual support and visible reputation. The
theoretical discussion draws on earlier qualitative and quantitative studies. Findings and implications. The
framework implies that moderation practices shape wellbeing outcomes. Limitations. The framework is untested
and needs empirical validation in future work. Framework. We distinguish three mechanisms: shared interest,
